model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 statutory revenue (core_metrics). The FFO margin path is struck on this base: FY25 FFO 1,187.5 / 2,685.0 = 44.2%.
inputs.share_count_basis: 5,222,977,091 stapled securities on issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 Trust 1/2/3 reports, note on contributed equity; the three trusts and the company are stapled 1:1). Held flat: FFO/DPS guidance is per security and already nets the DRP; the DRP cash it raises funds the capex charged in the flows. 31 August 2026 DRP issuance is not yet disclosed (FY2025 DRP added ~0.3%).
inputs.net_debt_note: HELD AT ZERO BY DESIGN. FFO is struck after net interest of A$822.1m (senior debt plus A$3,511.5m subordinated-note coupons), tax and NCI; capitalising a post-interest flow at the cost of equity and then deducting debt would charge the debt twice (ARG.NZ/IPL.NZ/PCT.NZ/GPT.AX/CHC.AX convention). Actual 31 Dec 2025: total interest-bearing debt A$14,894.7m (incl. A$3,511.5m subordinated notes), cash A$529.4m, gearing 30.4%, interest cover 3.4x (covenant 1.5x). 30 June 2026 (Group results release): gearing 35.5%, interest cover 3.6x, cost of debt 5.4%, FFO/debt 11.9%.
inputs.last_fcf_note: AFFO on the strict basis: FY25 FFO 1,187.5 less cash capital expenditure 360.5 (cash flow statement, FY2025 AR line 6852) less plant/equipment/intangibles 17.8 (line 6856). Capitalised financing costs (24.6) are already inside net interest via FFO. This is the FY0 anchor; the projection charges capex at 12.5% of revenue in base (see assumptions).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory OCF 1,052.5 less capex 378.3 (Metrics.csv). Not the valuation flow: statutory OCF is after interest, and FFO is the Group's own distributable-earnings measure (NAREIT basis, FY2025 AR page 53).
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payments (performance rights, Note 30 FY2025 AR: 17.3m rights on issue, ~A$13.5m fair value granted) are expensed inside the A$97.0m overheads line that FFO already deducts. Charging them again in the engine would double-count; SBC path set to zero and the house/street band collapses (SBC-zero convention).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY25 interest income A$17.3m is netted inside FFO net interest; no cash is added to EV, so there is nothing to strip.
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 (last audited Group consolidated balance sheet; the H1 FY2026 extract carries only the three stapled trusts' half-year statements, so 30 June 2026 Group gearing/cover are taken from the results release as summarised in the Analysis JSON)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC, because the flow is post-interest FFO/AFFO. Built in AUD: 10-year ACGB ~4.3%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~0.85 for a large A-REIT with 30-35% gearing and a A$3.5bn hybrid layer => 8.55%, used as 8.5%. One rate across scenarios; scenario risk is carried in the flows (margin, capex, growth, terminal cap), not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities (A$134.2m, ground leases) are immaterial against A$31bn of investment property; lease payments (A$10.9m) sit inside property expenses/net interest that FFO already deducts. No separate charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: External non-controlling interests (A$10.4m FY25) are deducted inside FFO ('Minority interest' line of the FFO table). Attributable-only flow, no bridge item.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine per SKILL.md's REIT row (IAS 40 fair-value stapled property group; statutory NPAT dominated by revaluations, e.g. FY25 A$1,778.5m statutory vs A$1,187.5m FFO). Engine mapping: revenue x 'ebitda_margin' = FFO (post-interest, post-tax, post-NCI); SBC, lease, D&A and cash-tax paths are zero because FFO already carries them; 'capex_pct_path' is the AFFO deduction (maintenance capex, tenant incentives and the equity-funded share of redevelopment); wacc field = cost of equity; net_debt = 0. AFFO CONTEXT: FY25 distributions A$923.1m (77.7% of FFO) plus cash capex A$378m exceeded FFO by ~A$115m, funded by A$2.2bn of JV sell-downs (50% Chermside, 19.9% Westfield Sydney) and gearing that rose to 35.5% by June 2026 - the distribution is not fully covered by AFFO on the all-in capex definition (~15.5c vs 17.7c paid), which is why base charges 12.5% of revenue rather than maintenance-only. FY2026 ANCHOR: H1 FFO A$612.4m (11.73c, +4.4%); full-year guidance upgraded 25 Aug 2026 to at least 23.79c FFO (+4.25%) and 18.473c DPS; comparable NOI +4.4%, occupancy 99.8%, releasing spreads +3.7%, rent escalations 5.5%, cost of debt 5.4% (from 5.7%). Model choice recorded for the memory line: first valuation of this ticker.

historical_growth.eps_note: Statutory EPS is revaluation noise (FY22 5.8c, FY23 3.4c, FY25 34.2c on the same rent roll); CAGRs not meaningful and not computed.
historical_growth.fcf_series: FFO per security (the distributable-earnings series this model capitalises): FY15 22.58c, FY16 23.30, FY17 24.29, FY18 25.24, FY19 25.42, FY20 14.76, FY21 16.64, FY22 20.06, FY23 21.11, FY24 21.82, FY25 22.82. Pre-COVID FY15-FY19 CAGR 3.0%; the 5-yr figure is COVID rebound, the 10-yr figure says FFO per security has gone nowhere since 2015.
historical_growth.dps_series: Distribution per security: FY15 20.90c ... FY19 22.60, FY20 7.00, FY21 14.25, FY22 15.75, FY23 16.60, FY24 17.20, FY25 17.72; FY26 guided 18.473. Still 18% below FY2019 after five years of growth.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FFO-per-security pre-COVID trend (3.0%) corroborated by the revenue 3-yr CAGR (3.0%); FY2026 guided 4.25%+ is treated as a year-one anchor that fades, not a run-rate. The 10-yr FFO/security CAGR of 0.1% caps terminal growth at 2.5%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (book value) CAGR 0.1-0.6% vs revenue 3.0-4.4%: book value is IAS 40 fair value (cap-rate driven, with the FY2020 A$3.7bn writedown) rather than retained earnings, so the equity CAGR is not a growth anchor for a REIT and was not used.
historical_growth.notes: FFO is the series this model discounts; owner-FCF-style adjustments (SBC, interest income) are already inside it. AFFO on the all-in capex definition grew from 600.6 (FY22) to 809.2 (FY25) mainly because capex fell from 439 to 378, not because FFO grew faster.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands on the upgraded guidance (revenue +4.5% at a flat 44.5% FFO margin = ~A$1,249m, ~23.9c vs >=23.79c guided), then growth fades from the guided 4%+ to the 3.0% pre-COVID FFO trend and to 2.5% in perpetuity, in line with a 10-year record of ~flat FFO per security. Margin held flat: NOI growth of ~4% is offset by the hedge book stepping down through 2029 (swap rate ~3.3% vs 5.4% marginal cost). AFFO deduction 12.5% of revenue: maintenance capex, tenant incentives and the equity-funded share of redevelopment, with the balance of the A$4bn pipeline funded by JV capital recycling as in 2025-26. Terminal 16x AFFO (below the 17.1x Gordon value at 8.5%/2.5%).

bull.narrative: Comparable NOI keeps compounding at 4-5% (99.8% occupancy, +3.7% spreads, 5.5% escalations, media/membership monetisation) and the RBA easing cycle takes the 5.4% cost of debt toward 4.8% as legacy notes refinance - each 25bp on ~A$11bn of net debt is ~A$27m of FFO, lifting the margin 150bp by year 5. Redevelopments (Bondi Level 6, Southland, Burwood) deliver 6-7% yields on cost and JV partners (ART, Dexus) keep funding the pipeline, so the equity capex charge settles at 10%. The 670ha land bank starts converting (Warringah, West Lakes, Hornsby dwellings) after year 5, supporting 3% terminal growth and an 18x exit.

bear.narrative: FY2026 still lands near guidance (H1 is banked), then a consumer slowdown flattens specialty sales and turnover rent for two years while the hedge book rolls off into a higher-for-longer curve: +100bp on ~A$11bn of net debt is ~A$110m (4% of revenue), taking the FFO margin from 44.5% to 41% by year 4. Post-Bondi coronial findings add mandated security cost. With gearing already 35.5%, JV sell-downs stall and the full historical capex run-rate (15% of revenue) is charged to equity; distributions are covered only by leaning on the balance sheet. Terminal growth 2%, exit 13x AFFO.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance met in FY2026, then FFO per security fades to its pre-COVID 3% trend and 2.5% terminal growth; FFO margin flat as NOI growth and hedge roll-off offset; AFFO after a 12.5%-of-revenue capex charge capitalised at 8.5% cost of equity with a 16x terminal cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: NOI compounding at 4-5% plus a falling cost of debt lifts the FFO margin 150bp; JV recycling keeps the equity capex charge at 10%; land-bank residential conversion supports 3% terminal growth and an 18x exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: Consumer slowdown plus hedge roll-off into higher rates compresses the FFO margin to 41%; all-in capex (15% of revenue) charged to equity as JV sell-downs stall at 35.5% gearing; 2% terminal growth, 13x exit.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: the flow is levered (A$822m interest on A$2,063m EBIT), the hedge book steps down through 2029, gearing has already moved from 30.4% to 35.5% in six months, and the FY2019-2025 record shows distributions still 18% below their prior peak. Bull cut to 25%: it needs rate cuts, sustained 4%+ NOI growth and a land-bank conversion that is years from cash, several independent things going right; the 10-year FFO/security CAGR is 0.1%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Scentre is valued as a stream of distributable earnings, not as an operating company: FFO (the Group's own NAREIT-basis measure, post-interest, post-tax, post-NCI) less an equity capex charge, capitalised at an 8.5% AUD cost of equity with no debt deduction. The FY2026 guidance year is anchored; everything after it fades to the ten-year record of roughly flat FFO per security. The key judgment is the capex charge: management's payout (78% of FFO) is only sustainable because JV sell-downs and rising gearing fund the difference, so the base case charges more than maintenance capex and the bear charges the full historical run-rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: each 50bp on the 8.5% moves the base value by roughly 8-9%; the sensitivity grid is the honest range.
Capex definition: maintenance-only (~10%) versus all-in (~15%) of revenue is a ~A$135m/yr swing in AFFO, about 15% of value.
Hedge roll-off through 2029: the FFO margin path assumes NOI growth absorbs the step-up; a higher-for-longer curve is the bear case.
Gearing at 35.5% with a A$3.5bn hybrid layer whose coupons reset; the model treats hybrids as debt (coupons inside FFO), consistent with the Group's FFO table.
Security/regulatory cost after the Bondi Junction coronial findings (Feb 2026) is unquantified by management and sits only in the bear margin path.
The DRP and any equity raise: securities held flat at 5,223m; a discounted raise to repair gearing would dilute per-security value.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3.275-4.27.
data_sources.financials: SCG.AX_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2015-FY2025); FY2025 Annual Report FFO table (page 53, lines 2964-3016), cash flow statement (lines 6845-6872), five-year summary (lines 3658-3672), Note 30 share-based payments, Note 11 NTA A$3.62; H1 FY2026 Trust 1/2/3 half-year reports (securities on issue 5,222,977,091 at 30 June 2026; guidance lines 1159-1166); FFO-per-security history from FY2019/FY2020 annual five-year summaries.
data_sources.qualitative: SCG.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-25): H1 2026 results (FFO A$612.4m/11.73c, gearing 35.5%, cover 3.6x, cost of debt 5.4%), Mt Gravatt 50% JV (A$882.5m), Bondi coronial findings, bull/bear axes.
